description: A member read and written like a field but backed by `get`/`set`/`init` accessors, replacing separate getter and setter methods.
`init` allows assignment only during construction, and `required` makes the compiler reject any object initializer that does not set the member.
C# 14 syntax that refers to a property's compiler-generated backing field, so one accessor can add logic without a hand-written private field.
An access level that limits a type or member to its own assembly (project), and the default for top-level types.
C# methods cannot be overridden unless marked `virtual`, a derived class replaces them with `override`, and `sealed` stops further derivation.
A class or struct with compiler-generated value equality, `ToString` and `with` copies, intended for data such as DTOs, messages and value objects.
A `with` expression that creates a shallow copy of a record with some properties changed, leaving the original untouched.
A contract with no instance state that a class or struct implements, used as the seam for dependency injection and test doubles.
